claims.text: CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational screening can simultaneously enhance phase stability, refine microstructure, and optimize properties in HEAs.
Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti is an example of a multi-principal-element HEA system suitable for high-throughput CALPHAD exploration.
HEAs designed without targeted computational guidance may initially have multiple phases and an unrefined microstructure.
A CALPHAD-based high-throughput approach can screen a wide HEA compositional space.
The high-throughput approach can screen processing parameters as well as compositions.
The screening can target single-phase solid-solution formation.
The screening can target specified precipitate fractions.
A composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element can be explored in the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system.
Screening should cover temperatures representative of fabrication and service environments.
CALPHAD predictions should subsequently be validated experimentally under identical processing conditions.
The desired mediator is a predicted dominant solid-solution phase containing 5–50 vol% strengthening L2₁ or ordered B2 precipitates.
CALPHAD uses thermodynamic databases and simulation to predict the balance between mixing-entropy and mixing-enthalpy contributions.
Those predictions guide alloy composition and processing routes that reduce unwanted phase formation.
CALPHAD-guided composition and processing promote a fine microstructure and optimal mechanical properties.
CALPHAD-designed HEAs will have improved high-temperature phase stability.
CALPHAD-designed HEAs will have a finer, more homogeneous microstructure with fewer detrimental phases.
CALPHAD-designed HEAs will have higher yield strength and ductility than conventionally designed HEAs.
Non-computationally designed HEAs may have multiple phases, coarser microstructures, and suboptimal properties because their compositions and processing parameters are not optimized.
The method's effectiveness is limited by thermodynamic-database accuracy, particularly for systems containing more than five elements.
Scaling is limited by computational time and experimental reproducibility.

contradictions.description: The intervention targets a single-phase solid solution, while the structural mediator specifies 5–50 vol% of distinct L2₁ or B2 precipitate phases. These targets are incompatible if intended to describe the same final microstructure rather than alternative design objectives.
